title: How the Professional Discussion works
blurb: The final NEBDN assessment: when you take it, how long it lasts, what it is based on and what happens if you need a resit.
question: Your colleague has just passed the NEBDN Knowledge Test, but two of her portfolio units are still waiting to be signed off. She wants to book the Professional Discussion for next week. Can she, and what should she expect on the day?

teach.body: The NEBDN Level 3 Diploma in Dental Nursing has three assessments: the Portfolio of Evidence, the Knowledge Test and the Professional Discussion. The Professional Discussion is the final one. You need a pass in all three to achieve the Diploma, and the Diploma is what lets you apply to join the GDC register as a dental nurse. Nothing is awarded until the Professional Discussion is passed.

teach.h: What the discussion is based on
teach.body: NEBDN says the discussion is based on the nine duties of the dental nurse, indicative of the dental nurse's role and in line with the GDC Scope of Practice. It draws on the knowledge and practical activities you have completed in your workplace. So it is not a quiz of facts. It is a professional conversation about what you actually do, why you do it that way, and how you stay within your role and the GDC's standards.

teach.caption: Both are set and externally marked by NEBDN. The portfolio, by contrast, is assessed by your provider and quality assured by NEBDN.

teach.h: Getting ready in the weeks before
items: Learn the nine duties well enough to explain each in your own words.
For every duty, pick at least two real examples from your own work and portfolio.
For each example, know why you acted as you did: the GDC standard, guidance or law behind it.
Check each example stays inside the dental nurse's scope of practice.
Practise talking it through out loud with your mentor or a colleague.
Follow your provider's and NEBDN's instructions for the online session, and set up a quiet, private space.

teach.text: The Professional Discussion is not a spoken Knowledge Test. Reciting textbook facts without saying what YOU did, why, and how it stayed within your scope does not show the assessor how you carry out the duties at work.

items: Final of three NEBDN assessments; only taken once the portfolio and Knowledge Test are passed.
60 minutes with an assessor plus 10 minutes reading time, online, pass or fail.
Based on the nine duties of the dental nurse, in line with the GDC Scope of Practice.
Draws on your real workplace activities, so your portfolio examples are your raw material.
Three additional resits are allowed; pass all three assessments to apply to the GDC register.

summary: You can now place the Professional Discussion in the Diploma journey, state its length, delivery, grading and resit rules, explain what it is based on, and separate what NEBDN has published from what it hasn't, so you prepare in the right way.

A.q: How long is the NEBDN Professional Discussion?
options: 90 minutes, with no separate reading time
45 minutes, plus 15 minutes reading time
60 minutes, plus 10 minutes reading time
30 minutes, plus 30 minutes reading time
A.why: NEBDN's specification describes a 60-minute assessment with 10 minutes reading time.

whyNot.0: 90 minutes is the length of the Knowledge Test, not the discussion.
whyNot.1: These timings are not in the NEBDN specification.
whyNot.3: The reading time is 10 minutes, and the discussion itself is 60 minutes.

A.q: A trainee has passed the Knowledge Test, but her portfolio is not yet signed off. When can she sit the Professional Discussion?
options: Only after the portfolio has also been passed
Straight away, as the Knowledge Test is passed
Before the portfolio, as it is assessed separately
Any time, as the order of assessments is flexible
A.why: The Professional Discussion is the final assessment and must only be taken after both the Portfolio of Evidence and the Knowledge Test are passed.

whyNot.1: Passing the Knowledge Test alone is not enough; the portfolio must be passed too.
whyNot.2: The portfolio must be passed before the discussion, not after it.
whyNot.3: The order is fixed: the discussion always comes last.

A.q: According to NEBDN, what is the Professional Discussion based on?
options: The nine principles of the GDC Standards only
The 65 topics covered by the Knowledge Test
A single clinical case chosen by the assessor on the day
The nine duties of the dental nurse, within GDC scope
A.why: NEBDN says it is based on the nine duties of the dental nurse, indicative of the role and in line with the GDC Scope of Practice.

whyNot.0: The GDC principles will support your answers, but NEBDN names the nine duties as the basis.
whyNot.1: The Knowledge Test has 65 questions; the discussion is not built on them.
whyNot.2: NEBDN has not said the discussion is a single clinical case chosen on the day.

B.q: How is the Professional Discussion carried out and marked?
options: Face to face at a test centre, marked by your mentor
Online with an assessor, externally marked by NEBDN
In your own surgery, observed and marked by your dentist
As a written essay, marked by your training provider
B.why: NEBDN's specification says it is completed with an assessor, carried out online, and set and externally marked by NEBDN.

whyNot.0: It is online, and your mentor does not mark it.
whyNot.2: It is not a workplace observation; that kind of evidence belongs in the portfolio.
whyNot.3: It is a spoken discussion, not an essay, and NEBDN marks it, not your provider.

B.q: A learner fails her first attempt at the Professional Discussion. What does the NEBDN specification allow?
options: One resit only, after a compulsory retraining course
No resits; she must restart the whole Diploma
Three additional resits of the discussion
Unlimited resits within the next twelve months
B.why: NEBDN permits three additional resits for the Professional Discussion, the same as for the Knowledge Test.

whyNot.0: NEBDN allows three additional resits, and a resit is defined as not needing additional learning.
whyNot.1: She does not restart the Diploma; resits are permitted.
whyNot.3: The number is limited to three additional resits.

B.q: Which of these has NEBDN NOT published about the Professional Discussion?
options: That it lasts 60 minutes with 10 minutes reading
That it is graded pass or fail
That it is carried out online with an assessor
The exact questions the assessor will ask
B.why: NEBDN publishes the format, length and grading, but not the questions. Prepare by knowing the duties and your own examples.

whyNot.0: The 60 minutes plus 10 minutes reading time is in the NEBDN specification.
whyNot.1: Pass or fail grading is in the specification.
whyNot.2: The specification says it is online and completed with an assessor.

C.q: How is the Professional Discussion graded?
options: Pass or fail
Distinction, merit, pass or fail
A percentage with a pass mark of 70%
A stanine score from 1 to 9
C.why: Like the Knowledge Test and the portfolio, the Professional Discussion is graded pass or fail.

whyNot.1: There are no merit or distinction grades in the NEBDN Diploma.
whyNot.2: NEBDN does not publish a percentage pass mark for the discussion.
whyNot.3: Stanines are not used in NEBDN assessments.

C.q: Your mentor asks where your discussion examples should mainly come from. What is the best answer?
options: Model answers memorised from online forums
Activities you have completed in your workplace
Case studies taken from your course textbook
Situations you imagine might happen to you one day
C.why: NEBDN says the discussion is based on knowledge and practical activities completed in the workplace that relate to the nine duties.

whyNot.0: Memorised answers don't show what you actually do, and NEBDN does not publish the questions.
whyNot.2: Textbook cases can support your knowledge, but the discussion is about your own practice.
whyNot.3: Hypothetical situations are weaker than real things you have done and reflected on.

C.q: A learner passes the Professional Discussion, having already passed the portfolio and Knowledge Test. What can she do next?
options: Start diagnosing patients under supervision
Sit an extra NEBDN oral exam on scope
Apply to join the GDC register
Resit the discussion to improve her grade
C.why: Passing all three assessments achieves the Diploma, and those who achieve it can apply to register with the GDC as a dental nurse.

whyNot.0: Dental nurses do not diagnose disease, registered or not.
whyNot.1: There is no further oral exam; the discussion is the final assessment.
whyNot.3: Resits cannot be taken to improve a grade, only after a fail.

reteach.title: Think of it like learning to drive
reteach.question: If the Diploma were a driving licence, which part would the Professional Discussion be?

blocks.body: Learner drivers log supervised lessons, pass a theory test, then take a practical test. The Diploma works the same way. Your portfolio is the logbook of supervised practice. The Knowledge Test is the theory test. The Professional Discussion is the practical test, except that instead of driving you talk the assessor through how you actually do the job: what you did, why, and how you kept within the rules of the road (your scope and the GDC's standards).

blocks.text: You can't take the practical test before passing the theory, and you can't take the Professional Discussion before passing both the portfolio and the Knowledge Test.

explain.body: The Professional Discussion is the last of three NEBDN assessments. It must only be taken after the Portfolio of Evidence and the Knowledge Test have been passed.

test.q: Which assessment is the final one in the NEBDN Diploma?
options: The Knowledge Test
The Portfolio of Evidence
The Professional Discussion
The GDC registration interview
test.why: The Professional Discussion is the final assessment, taken after the portfolio and Knowledge Test are passed.

whyNot.0: The Knowledge Test must be passed before the discussion.
whyNot.1: The portfolio must also be passed before the discussion.
whyNot.3: There is no GDC registration interview; you apply once you hold the Diploma.

explain.body: 60 minutes with an assessor, plus 10 minutes reading time. It is online, set and externally marked by NEBDN, and graded pass or fail.

test.q: How much reading time does NEBDN give before the 60-minute discussion?
options: None
5 minutes
15 minutes
10 minutes
test.why: The specification gives 10 minutes reading time alongside the 60-minute discussion.

explain.body: The nine duties of the dental nurse, in line with the GDC Scope of Practice, using the knowledge and practical activities you have completed at work.

test.q: Which document sets the boundaries that every discussion answer must stay within?
options: The GDC Scope of Practice
The practice's staff handbook
The NHS dental contract
The Knowledge Test syllabus
test.why: NEBDN says the discussion is in line with the Scope of Practice set out by the GDC.

whyNot.1: A staff handbook covers local rules, not your professional boundaries.
whyNot.2: The NHS contract covers funding and delivery, not your scope.
whyNot.3: The Knowledge Test syllabus is not what NEBDN names for the discussion.

explain.body: Three additional resits are allowed. A resit means taking it again without additional learning being required. You cannot resit a pass to improve it.

test.q: How many additional resits of the Professional Discussion does NEBDN permit?
test.why: NEBDN permits three additional resits for the Professional Discussion.

whyNot.0: The specification allows three, not one.
whyNot.1: The specification allows three, not two.
whyNot.3: The specification allows three, not five.
